two-sum.approach: Iterate through the array, storing each number's index in a hash map. For each element, check if the complement (target - num) already exists in the map.

contains-duplicate.approach: Insert each element into a HashSet. If insertion fails (element already exists), a duplicate is found.

valid-anagram.approach: Count character frequencies using an array of size 26. Compare frequency arrays for both strings.

group-anagrams.approach: Sort each string to create a canonical key and group strings with the same key using a hash map.

top-k-frequent-elements.approach: Count frequencies with a hash map, then use bucket sort where index = frequency to get top-k in O(n).

product-of-array-except-self.approach: Build prefix products left-to-right in the output array, then multiply suffix products right-to-left in a second pass.

valid-sudoku.approach: Use hash sets to track seen numbers in each row, column, and 3×3 box. Return false on any duplicate.

longest-consecutive-sequence.approach: Add all numbers to a set. For each number that is the start of a sequence (num-1 not in set), count consecutive elements.

best-time-to-buy-and-sell-stock.approach: Track the minimum price seen so far. At each step, compute profit = price - minPrice and update maxProfit.

valid-parentheses.approach: Push opening brackets onto a stack. For closing brackets, check the top matches. Stack must be empty at the end.

min-stack.approach: Maintain a secondary stack tracking the current minimum. Push to min stack when the new value ≤ current min.

evaluate-reverse-polish-notation.approach: Push numbers onto a stack. When an operator is encountered, pop two operands, apply the operator, push the result.

generate-parentheses.approach: Recursively build strings by adding '(' if open < n, and ')' if close < open. Base case: length == 2n.

daily-temperatures.approach: Use a decreasing monotonic stack of indices. Pop elements when a warmer temperature is found and compute differences.

car-fleet.approach: Sort cars by position descending. Calculate arrival times; a car forms a new fleet if it arrives later than the current fleet leader.

largest-rectangle-in-histogram.approach: Use an increasing stack of indices. When a shorter bar is found, pop and calculate area using the popped height and width span.

binary-search.approach: Maintain left and right pointers. Compare mid element to target; halve the search space each iteration.

search-a-2d-matrix.approach: Treat the 2D matrix as a flattened sorted array. Apply standard binary search, converting 1D index to 2D coordinates.

koko-eating-bananas.approach: Binary search on eating speed k. For each k, check if Koko can finish all piles within h hours. Minimize k.

find-minimum-in-rotated-sorted-array.approach: Binary search comparing mid to right. If mid > right, minimum is in the right half; otherwise it's in the left half.

search-in-rotated-sorted-array.approach: Determine which half is sorted. If target is in the sorted half, search there; otherwise search the other half.

valid-palindrome.approach: Use left and right pointers, skip non-alphanumeric chars, compare characters case-insensitively moving inward.

two-sum-ii-input-array-is-sorted.approach: Left and right pointers. If sum < target, move left forward; if sum > target, move right backward.

3sum.approach: Sort the array. Fix one element, then use two pointers on the remaining subarray to find pairs summing to -fixed.

container-with-most-water.approach: Start with widest container (left=0, right=n-1). Move the shorter pointer inward to potentially find a taller line.

trapping-rain-water.approach: Track leftMax and rightMax. Move the pointer with the smaller max inward, accumulating water = max - height at each step.

best-time-to-buy-and-sell-stock-ii.approach: Add every positive price difference (prices[i] - prices[i-1]) since we can make unlimited transactions.

longest-substring-without-repeating-char.approach: Expand right pointer, add char to set. If duplicate, shrink from left until no duplicate. Track max window size.

longest-repeating-character-replacement.approach: Track character frequencies in window. If windowSize - maxFreq > k, shrink from left. Track max window size.

permutation-in-string.approach: Use a fixed-size window equal to s1's length. Compare character frequency arrays of window and s1.

minimum-window-substring.approach: Expand right to include all chars of t. Once valid, shrink from left to minimize. Track the smallest valid window.

reverse-linked-list.approach: Maintain prev, curr, next pointers. Reverse each link by pointing curr.next to prev, then advance all three.

merge-two-sorted-lists.approach: Use a dummy head. Compare nodes from both lists, append the smaller one, advance that pointer. Append remaining.

linked-list-cycle.approach: Use slow (1 step) and fast (2 steps) pointers. If they meet, there's a cycle. If fast reaches null, no cycle.

reorder-list.approach: Find mid with slow/fast pointers. Reverse the second half. Interleave-merge both halves.

remove-nth-node-from-end-of-list.approach: Advance fast pointer n steps ahead. Then move both until fast reaches end. Slow is at the node before target.

copy-list-with-random-pointer.approach: First pass: create a map of original → copy nodes. Second pass: set next and random pointers using the map.

lru-cache.approach: Hash map for O(1) lookup, doubly linked list for O(1) insert/remove. Move accessed nodes to head; evict from tail.

merge-k-sorted-lists.approach: Push head of each list into a min-heap. Pop smallest, append to result, push its next node. Repeat until heap empty.

invert-binary-tree.approach: Recursively swap left and right children of every node. Base case: null node.

maximum-depth-of-binary-tree.approach: Return 1 + max(depth(left), depth(right)). Base case: null returns 0.

same-tree.approach: Recursively check if both nodes have the same value and their left/right subtrees are identical.

subtree-of-another-tree.approach: For each node in the main tree, check if the subtree rooted there is identical to the target tree.

lowest-common-ancestor-of-a-binary-searc.approach: If both values < node, go left. If both > node, go right. Otherwise, current node is the LCA.

binary-tree-level-order-traversal.approach: Use a queue. Process all nodes at current level (queue size), add their children. Collect each level's values.

validate-binary-search-tree.approach: Pass min/max bounds recursively. Each node's value must be within (min, max). Update bounds at each level.

kth-smallest-element-in-a-bst.approach: Inorder traversal visits BST nodes in sorted order. Count nodes visited; return when count == k.

construct-binary-tree-from-preorder-and-.approach: First preorder element is root. Find root in inorder to split left/right subtrees. Recurse on each half.

binary-tree-maximum-path-sum.approach: At each node, compute max single-path sum (node + max(left, right, 0)). Update global max with node+left+right.

serialize-and-deserialize-binary-tree.approach: Preorder traversal with null markers for serialization. Deserialize by consuming tokens sequentially.

implement-trie-prefix-tree.approach: Each node has a children map (26 chars) and isEnd flag. Insert/search by traversing character by character.

word-search.approach: From each cell, DFS in 4 directions matching word characters. Mark visited cells to avoid reuse; backtrack on failure.

word-search-ii.approach: Build a trie from all words. DFS from each cell guided by trie nodes. Prune branches with no trie children.

number-of-islands.approach: Iterate grid. On finding '1', increment count and flood-fill (DFS/BFS) to mark all connected land as visited.

clone-graph.approach: Use a hash map of original → clone. BFS/DFS traverse the graph, cloning nodes and connecting neighbors.

pacific-atlantic-water-flow.approach: BFS/DFS from Pacific edges and Atlantic edges separately. Answer = cells reachable from both oceans.

course-schedule.approach: Build adjacency list. Detect cycle using DFS with 3 states (unvisited, visiting, visited). No cycle → possible.

course-schedule-ii.approach: Use Kahn's algorithm: process nodes with in-degree 0. Add to result, decrement neighbors' in-degrees. Repeat.

rotting-oranges.approach: Add all rotten oranges to queue. BFS level by level (each level = 1 minute). Count minutes until no fresh oranges remain.

climbing-stairs.approach: dp[i] = dp[i-1] + dp[i-2]. Only need two previous values, so use two variables instead of an array.

min-cost-climbing-stairs.approach: dp[i] = cost[i] + min(dp[i-1], dp[i-2]). Optimize space with two variables.

house-robber.approach: dp[i] = max(dp[i-1], dp[i-2] + nums[i]). Can't rob adjacent houses. Track two previous values.

house-robber-ii.approach: Run House Robber twice: once on nums[0..n-2], once on nums[1..n-1]. Take the max of both results.

longest-palindromic-substring.approach: For each index, expand outward for both odd and even length palindromes. Track the longest found.

palindromic-substrings.approach: For each center (2n-1 centers), expand while chars match. Count each valid expansion as a palindromic substring.

decode-ways.approach: dp[i] = dp[i-1] (if valid single digit) + dp[i-2] (if valid two-digit 10-26). Handle '0' as special case.

coin-change.approach: dp[i] = min coins to make amount i. For each coin, dp[i] = min(dp[i], dp[i-coin] + 1). Init dp[0]=0.

maximum-product-subarray.approach: Track both max and min products ending at current position (negatives can flip). Update global max each step.

word-break.approach: dp[i] = true if s[0..i) can be segmented. For each i, check all j < i: dp[j] && s[j..i) in wordDict.

longest-increasing-subsequence.approach: Maintain a tails array. For each num, binary search for its position. Replace or extend the tails array.

unique-paths.approach: dp[i][j] = dp[i-1][j] + dp[i][j-1]. First row and column are all 1s. Can optimize to 1D array.

longest-common-subsequence.approach: If chars match, dp[i][j] = dp[i-1][j-1]+1. Otherwise, dp[i][j] = max(dp[i-1][j], dp[i][j-1]).

maximum-subarray.approach: Track current sum; reset to current element if sum becomes negative. Update global max at each step.

jump-game.approach: Track the farthest reachable index. At each step, update farthest = max(farthest, i + nums[i]). Fail if i > farthest.

merge-intervals.approach: Sort by start time. Iterate and merge overlapping intervals (current.start ≤ prev.end). Extend end if needed.

insert-interval.approach: Add all intervals before new. Merge overlapping ones with new interval. Add all intervals after. Three phases.

non-overlapping-intervals.approach: Sort by end time. Greedily keep intervals that don't overlap with the last kept interval. Count removals.

meeting-rooms-ii.approach: Sort by start time. Use a min-heap of end times. If earliest end ≤ current start, reuse room. Else add new room.

rotate-image.approach: Transpose the matrix (swap [i][j] with [j][i]), then reverse each row. This rotates 90° clockwise in-place.

spiral-matrix.approach: Maintain top, bottom, left, right boundaries. Traverse right→down→left→up, shrinking boundaries after each direction.

set-matrix-zeroes.approach: Use first row and first column as markers. Scan matrix, mark rows/cols to zero. Then zero out using markers.

kth-largest-element-in-an-array.approach: Use Quickselect (partition-based). Partition around a pivot; recurse on the half containing the k-th element.

find-median-from-data-stream.approach: Maintain a max-heap (lower half) and min-heap (upper half). Balance sizes after each insert. Median from heap tops.

design-twitter.approach: Hash maps for follows and tweets. Merge-k-sorted approach using a heap for the news feed of followed users.

task-scheduler.approach: Count frequencies. Slots = (maxFreq-1)*(n+1) + count_of_max_freq_tasks. Answer = max(slots, total tasks).

combination-sum.approach: Sort candidates. Backtrack: add current candidate (can reuse), recurse with remaining target. Skip if exceeds target.

subsets.approach: For each element, choose to include or exclude it. Recursively build all 2ⁿ subsets.

permutations.approach: Swap each element to the current position, recurse on the remaining. Use a visited set or swap-based approach.

letter-combinations-of-a-phone-number.approach: Map digits to letters. For each digit, try all mapped letters and recurse to the next digit.

n-queens.approach: Place queens row by row. Track columns and diagonals with sets. Backtrack when no valid column exists.

number-of-1-bits.approach: Count set bits using n & (n-1) which clears the lowest set bit. Count iterations until n becomes 0.

counting-bits.approach: dp[i] = dp[i >> 1] + (i & 1). Each number's bit count = right-shifted value's count + last bit.

reverse-bits.approach: Iterate 32 times. Shift result left, add last bit of n (n & 1), shift n right.

missing-number.approach: XOR all indices (0..n) with all array elements. Duplicate values cancel out, leaving the missing number.

sum-of-two-integers.approach: XOR gives sum without carry. AND + left shift gives carry. Repeat until carry is 0.

reverse-integer.approach: Extract last digit with % 10, build reversed number. Check overflow before multiplying by 10.

happy-number.approach: Compute sum of squared digits. Use slow/fast pointers to detect cycles. If it reaches 1, it's happy.

plus-one.approach: Start from the last digit. If digit < 9, increment and return. If 9, set to 0 and carry. Handle all-9s case.

pow-x-n.approach: If n is even: x^n = (x^(n/2))^2. If n is odd: x^n = x * x^(n-1). Handle negative n by inverting x.

median-of-two-sorted-arrays.approach: Binary search on the shorter array's partition point. Ensure left halves ≤ right halves across both arrays.

edit-distance.approach: dp[i][j] = min operations to convert word1[0..i) to word2[0..j). Three operations: insert, delete, replace.

regular-expression-matching.approach: dp[i][j] = does s[0..i) match p[0..j). Handle '.' (any char) and '*' (zero or more of preceding char).
